fields.description:
## Problem

`infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/handler.py` prices CloudWatch token counts
using a rate table derived daily from Cost Explorer and matched to models by
string heuristics. In the twelve days since the cap was deployed (2026-09-12)
that layer produced four defects, all one class — matching model identifiers to
billing labels by substring and suffix: a direction-suffix collision in
`_rate_for`/`_match`, where candidate `input-token-count` also matches
`...-cache-write-input-token-count` and the longest match wins, so input resolves
to cache-write for any ModelId without a version suffix; a `_normalise` mismatch
where label `Nova2.0Lite` and id `us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0` normalise so that
neither contains the other, dropping the model to `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K`; the
`BEDROCK_SERVICE_VALUES` allowlist from 3083-ada3-3a0f-4051 omitting five live
services, leaving the CE signal at about a third of real spend; and
`MARKETPLACE_TOKEN_SUFFIXES` handling only CamelCase, silently skipping the
snake_case and `_Global` usage types AWS also bills. Two of the four reached
production unalarmed, one for seven days.

## Approach

Delete the pricing-derivation layer. Price every token at a ceiling rate for its
direction, set above the highest per-direction rate observed on this account, so
the estimate is an upper bound and the cap cannot fire late. Per UTC day:

    spend = max( sum over regions and the four token metrics of
                   undimensioned CloudWatch Sum * CEILING[metric],
                 ce_spend )

The estimate reads exactly the four undimensioned Sum aggregates per region and
never adds per-ModelId series to that total; per-ModelId data is read only for the
warn/trip log line. Today's handler reads only per-ModelId series precisely
because mixing the two double-counts.

Cost Explorer stays in enforcement: it is the only signal covering Bedrock spend
that publishes no token metric (Cohere Rerank is live; provisioned throughput and
batch are structural), and it is orthogonal to all four defects.

**Release discriminator.** An all-empty CloudWatch read is ambiguous: it is both a
metrics gap and the normal idle/new-UTC-day state the automatic release depends
on. Empty alone is therefore never treated as unavailable. The cap may release on
an empty read only when CE for that day is available and zero; if CE is nonzero or
unavailable, the deny is held. A partial-region failure holds the deny, because
the surviving region's total is a floor, not the account total.

**Accepted limitation.** Ceiling pricing over-estimates for models much cheaper
than the priciest — the cheapest here are two orders of magnitude below, and two
bill nothing for cache-write, so the factor is unbounded. A large embedding or
small-model batch job can trip the cap at a small fraction of intended spend.
Accepted for simplicity; the remedy if it bites is an exact-match
`{ModelId: rate}` override defaulting to the ceiling, equality only.

## Figures

Machine-local policy bars spend totals and bill figures from the tracker, because
the tickets branch auto-pushes to the public GitHub mirror. Values are in the
operator's local-only note
`~/Desktop/bedrock-cap-redesign-local-only/design.md`, present on the implementing
workstation, and reproducible without it: each CEILING entry is 1.25x the highest
per-token rate for that direction across all Bedrock services in the trailing 60
days of CE, and the threshold is the intended daily cap scaled by the median
over-estimate factor over the same window.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The seven pricing functions (`_refresh_rates`, `_rate_for`, `_seed_for`,
  `_normalise`, `_strip_billing_region`, `_marketplace_rate_key`,
  `_rate_key_for_ce_group`) and six constants (`SEED_RATES`, `RATE_OVERRIDES`,
  `BEDROCK_SERVICE_VALUES`, `MARKETPLACE_TOKEN_SUFFIXES`, `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K`,
  `MARKETPLACE_TOKENS_PER_RATE_UNIT`) are absent. Checked: a test asserting no
  such name survives.
- [ ] The `TOKEN_METRICS` direction multipliers are removed. Checked: same test.
- [ ] `_metered_spend` issues exactly four undimensioned `GetMetricData` queries
  per region. Checked: a test asserting the stub recorded four per region.
- [ ] `_metered_spend` calls no `list_metrics` on the enforcement path. Checked:
  a test asserting zero such calls during a tick.
- [ ] A `CEILING` mapping gives one rate per token metric, each at least the
  highest for that direction in the fixture. Checked: a test comparing against
  rates derived from the fixture.
- [ ] Enforcement compares `max(ceiling_estimate, ce_spend)`. Checked: a test
  driving each arm larger in turn.
- [ ] `_ce_spend_today` classifies by predicate (service equals `Amazon Bedrock`
  or ends with the Bedrock Edition suffix), not an allowlist. Checked: a test
  proving it matches every Bedrock service in the fixture, including the five
  omitted.
- [ ] On an all-empty CloudWatch read the cap releases only when CE that day is
  available and zero. Checked: two tests — CE zero releases, CE nonzero holds.
- [ ] On an all-empty read with CE unavailable the deny is held. Checked: a test
  stubbing a CE exception.
- [ ] A partial-region failure holds the deny. Checked: a test raising in one
  region while the other returns data below threshold.
- [ ] Any exception from a metered or CE read fails closed. Checked: a test
  raising from each client in turn.
- [ ] `infra/terraform/bedrock_spend_cap.tf` carries the threshold and warning
  values from the design note. Checked: `terraform plan`.
- [ ] The orphaned `SEED_RATES`, `RATE_OVERRIDES`, `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K` and
  `RATE_WINDOW_DAYS` environment entries are deleted, with their `variable` and
  `locals` blocks. Checked: `terraform plan` shows exactly those deletions plus
  the threshold and warning changes.
- [ ] No unused Terraform declarations remain. Checked: `terraform validate`.
- [ ] `state["rates"]`, `state["rates_day"]`, `metered_estimated`, `MeteredRate`
  and the `" (estimated)"` rendering are removed. Checked: a test asserting the
  persisted state carries no rate table.
- [ ] A daily guard compares the estimate for a settled day against CE and raises
  an SNS warning when the estimate is below actual. Checked: a test driving a
  violation.
- [ ] That guard cannot attach or detach the policy. Checked: same test asserting
  no IAM call.
- [ ] Per-model token counts are logged on warn and trip paths only. Checked: a
  test asserting the line on trip, absent on a normal tick.
- [ ] CE and `list_metrics` fixtures are committed with structure recorded from
  this account but synthetic amounts, since the repo is public. Checked: a test
  asserting no fixture amount matches billing.
- [ ] The CE fixture retains CamelCase, snake_case, `_Global` and a non-token
  usage type. Checked: a test asserting each shape is present.
- [ ] Every ModelId in the `list_metrics` fixture is priced by the ceiling with no
  fallback path. Checked: a property test over the fixture.
- [ ] The README no longer describes bill-derived rates, the seed fallback order
  or `UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K`. Checked: a test asserting those strings are absent.
- [ ] The README states the accepted over-estimate, the effective-cap band
  qualitatively, and that the figure is an upper bound. Checked: reading it.

## Testing

- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py -q`
  proves every criterion naming a test.
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint`, `make typecheck`, then `make verify`
  before push per AGENTS.md.
- `python3 scripts/terraform_prod.py plan --out <scratch>/plan.tfplan` must show
  exactly the env deltas above before any apply.

## Rollback

Immediate mitigation: set `DRY_RUN=true`, halting attach and detach while leaving
the function observable. Full back-out: revert the Gerrit change and re-run the
mediated plan and apply; Terraform packages the handler by content hash, so the
revert restores prior code and env exactly.
